paper_verdict.estimator_family: panel fixed effects OLS (country and year FE) with FMOLS, DOLS and PCSE robustness; spatial panel models for spillovers
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Outcome GTFP is a Malmquist-Luenberger/super-SBM green productivity index (growth-type), not labor productivity or GDP; exposure is a composite digital economy index (0-1 scale) so coefficients are not in comparable units. Estimates are mostly negative and several columns include a quadratic term (DE and DE2), so linear coefficients are not marginal effects. Many estimates come from the same sample (OLS/FMOLS/PCSE/DOLS/lags/subsamples) and are not independent. Income-group split has a tiny low-income cell (N=16) and annual WB reclassification. Belt and Road countries only. Reverse causality: no instruments; only lags of DE and FMOLS/DOLS endogeneity corrections.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: panel fixed effects (country FE, year FE) growth regression in log differences, country-clustered robust SEs; no IV/GMM
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Exposure is growth of ICT capital services per worker (capital deepening, log change x100), an input-growth elasticity rather than technology adoption; outcome is labor productivity growth (log change x100). The four informality proxies (VA share, vulnerable, agricultural, self employment) give four re-estimates on the same sample, so they are not independent, and subsamples (advanced, emerging) overlap with the global sample. Interaction terms (ΔINF x ln kIT) are conditional effects and should not be pooled with main effects. Authors argue reverse causality is mitigated by using growth rates/first differences (footnote 9) and say no suitable instrument exists. Country counts per regression are not given separately; 118/80/38 are sample totals (2374/1583/791 observations).
